rules/why: Since powers add when exponentials multiply, ln turns a product into a sum. e squared times e cubed is e to the five, so its ln is five: two plus three, the ln of each factor, added.
rules/rule: The same holds for any positive numbers a and b: ln of a times b is ln a plus ln b.
rules/nums: ln two is about zero point six nine and ln three about one point one, so ln six is their sum, one point seven nine.
rules/nine: A power is a product of equal factors. Nine is three times three, so ln nine is ln three plus ln three: two ln three, about two point two.
rules/power: So for any power k, ln of a to the k is k times ln a: the power comes out in front.
quot/flip: Two times a half is one, and ln one is zero. So ln two plus ln a half is zero: ln of a half is minus ln two, about minus zero point six nine. One over a number flips the sign of its log.
quot/quot: Dividing by two is multiplying by a half. So ln of three halves is ln three plus ln a half, which is ln three minus ln two: about one point one minus zero point six nine, zero point four one.
quot/diff: The log of a quotient is the difference of the logs: ln of a over b is ln a minus ln b.
quot/small: So minus the log of a number below one is positive: minus ln of a half is zero point six nine. The bigger a number p, the smaller minus ln p: minus ln of zero point nine is only zero point one one.
quot/try: Try one. Use ln two is about zero point six nine and ln five is about one point six one. Let p be one tenth. What is minus ln p?
quot/solve: Ten is two times five, so ln ten is zero point six nine plus one point six one: two point three oh. One over ten flips the sign of its log, so minus ln p is two point three oh. The smaller p, the taller the bar.
